exported_sections_exact.Definition:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A symmetrizable Cartan datum and its root lattice $Q$; the displayed symbols and relations are formed over $\mathbb Q(q)$.

[F1] The root lattice is freely generated by the simple roots, and $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for $h\in P^{\vee}$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], [[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]).

[F2] $q_i=q^{d_i}$ with $d_i>0$, so $q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F3] The tensor algebra is a direct sum of finite words with concatenation product; assigning group degrees to its generator symbols gives the direct-sum grading by total degree. A linear map from the generating vector space extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]).

[F4] The two-sided ideal generated by the listed relations is an ideal, its quotient ring is defined by cosets, and maps whose kernel contains that ideal factor uniquely through the quotient ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]], [[def-quotient-ring]], [[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

exported_sections_exact.Definition:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category and use
$H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$ and the object-level integer $\chi_0(M,N)$ from
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]]. For a basis object $R$, let
$P^R_{M,N}$ count endpoint-labelled exact sequences
$0\to N\to R\to M\to0$, and put $a_R=|\operatorname{Aut}(R)|$. Define the
**coefficientwise completed tensor space**
$$ H_{\mathcal A,\nu}\widehat\otimes H_{\mathcal A,\nu} =\prod_{([M],[N])}\mathbb Q(\nu)\,([M]\otimes[N]), $$
the space of all coefficient functions on ordered pairs of isomorphism
classes. Define the Green coproduct and counit by
$$ \Delta'([R])=\sum_{[M],[N]} \nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\frac{P^R_{M,N}}{a_R}[M]\otimes[N], \qquad \epsilon([R])=\begin{cases}1,&R\cong0,\\0,&R\not\cong0.\end{cases} $$
Each coefficient is finite; the sum need not have finite support. On finite
pure tensors define the **Euler-twisted tensor multiplication** by
$$ ([X]\otimes[Y])\cdot([Z]\otimes[W]) =\nu^{\chi_0(Y,Z)+\chi_0(Z,Y)}([X]\star[Z])\otimes([Y]\star[W]). $$
It is extended to completed tensors only when every output coefficient is a
finite sum. No algebra structure on the whole completion is asserted; this
finite-convergence condition is proved for products of Green images below.

exported_sections_exact.Definition:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$; the algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with its root grading and subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$; the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1$ and the indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$; and the divided powers $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

[F1] $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_S$ ($S=\{t^k:k\ge0\}$) has the universal property: for every ring with unit $B$ and every unit $u\in B$ there is a unique unital ring homomorphism $\Lambda_1\to B$ with $t\mapsto u$; every element of $\Lambda_1$ has a unique finite expansion $\sum_ka_kt^k$ with $a_k\in\mathbb Z$; and the sum-of-coefficients map $\varepsilon\colon\Lambda_1\to\mathbb Z$ is a unital ring homomorphism ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]).

[F2] $q$ is an indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$: $\mathbb Q(q)$ is the fraction field of $\mathbb Q[q]$, and no nonzero polynomial over $\mathbb Q$ vanishes at $q$; $q_i=q^{d_i}$ with $d_i>0$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

[F3] $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is graded by $Q=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$, $\deg K_h=0$, and $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_\beta U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is a direct sum; $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the commutative group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$, so $U_q^0$ is commutative and $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$, $K_0=1$; and $U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspace for every $\beta$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F4] $[m]_i!=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i\ne0$ for every $m\ge0$, $x^{(1)}=x$ and $x^{(0)}=1$, and $[m]_i=(q_i^m-q_i^{-m})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F5] The subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ are generated by the $F_i$, the $K_h$, and the $E_i$ respectively, and these elements together generate $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ as a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra; the rank-one subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ is described by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] (used only as the published divided-power convention reference) ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]], [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F6] A subring of a field is a domain; if $M$ is an $A$-submodule of a $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space and $0\ne d\in A$, then $m\mapsto m\otimes d^{-1}$ identifies $M$ with its image modulo the evident relation, and the canonical map $M\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$, $\sum_im_i\otimes s_i\mapsto\sum_is_im_i$, is injective: writing $s_i=a_id^{-1}$ with $a_i\in A$ and $0\ne d\in A$, the relation $\sum_ia_im_i=0$ follows from the vanishing of $\sum_is_im_i$ by multiplying by $d$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] for the coefficient calculus).

exported_sections_exact.Definition:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A symmetrizable Cartan datum with $q$ indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$, and an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra.

[F1] The datum has $q_i=q^{d_i}$ with positive integer $d_i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

[F2] The asymmetric $q$-integer and $q$-factorial are $[m]_t=1+t+\cdots+t^{m-1}$ and $[m]_t!=\prod_{j=1}^m[j]_t$, with $[0]_t=0$ and $[0]_t!=1$; the $q$-multinomial is the factorial quotient ([[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]).

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_q$. If $Q$ has oriented
cycles, take the abelian category of finite-dimensional nilpotent
representations; if $Q$ is acyclic, take all finite-dimensional
representations. In either case the indicated representation category is
essentially small; let $\mathcal A_Q$ be the explicit small skeleton
constructed in the proof. This skeleton is a finite-field hereditary Hall
category. Its simple objects
are $S_i$, $K_0\cong\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$ by dimension vector, and
$\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(S_i,S_j)=c_{ij}$ for arrows $i\to j$.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite loopless quiver $Q$, the finite field $k=\mathbb F_q$, and the category of its finite-dimensional nilpotent representations. Nilpotent means that some integer $n\geq1$ kills the composite along every path of length $n$.

[F1] The target Hall-category conditions are those of [[def-finite-field-hereditary-hall-category]] and [[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]. In particular, heredity here means vanishing of endpoint-fixed Yoneda two-extension classes, rather than a resolution assertion.

[F2] A two-fold splice is zero if its second short extension is the pushout of an extension by the first middle object ([[lem-yext-zero-splice-factorization]]).

[F3] The Grothendieck-group relation is $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for each short exact sequence ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]). Baer addition is the diagonal-pullback/codiagonal-pushout operation of [[def-baer-sum-of-extension-classes]] and [[thm-baer-sum-makes-extension-classes-an-abelian-group]].

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
Work in ZF. Let $I$ be finite and nonempty and $a=(a_{ij})$ a symmetric generalized Cartan matrix. Also allow $I=\varnothing$ by taking each half to be the coefficient field and its integral subalgebra to be $A$. Set $A=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, $k=\mathbb Q(t)$ and $S=k\langle f_i:i\in I\rangle/(s_{ij}:i\ne j)$, where, for $m=1-a_{ij}$,
$$s_{ij}=\sum_{r=0}^{m}(-1)^r\binom mr_t f_i^{m-r}f_jf_i^r.$$
Identify $S$ with the actual negative Drinfeld–Jimbo half by the choice-free crossed-double lemma, and let $U_A^-$ be its actual divided-power subalgebra. There exists a unique homogeneous bilinear form $B_t$ with $B_t(1,1)=1$ and
$$B_t(f_i x,y)=B_t(x,D_i y),\qquad D_i(f_jy)=\delta_{ij}y+t^{-a_{ij}}f_jD_i(y),\qquad D_i(1)=0.$$
It is symmetric. For ordinary words $u=f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_h}$ and $v=f_{j_1}\cdots f_{j_h}$ its value is
$$B_t(u,v)=\sum_{\pi:\,j_{\pi(b)}=i_b}t^{-\sum_{b<c,\,\pi(b)>\pi(c)}a_{i_b i_c}},$$
where the sum is over matching permutations. In particular ordinary-word values lie in $A$, and values on $U_A^-$ lie in the localization of $A$ obtained by inverting the symmetric quantum factorials.

For any $\alpha\in\mathbb N^I$, including $\alpha=0$, enumerate the finite set $W_\alpha$ of ordinary words of that degree, and let $G_\alpha(t)$ be their Gram matrix in the displayed formula. At every real $c>0$,
$$\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q(c)}G_\alpha(c)\le\operatorname{rank}_{k}G_\alpha(t)\le\dim_k S[\alpha]\le p_\alpha,$$
where $p_\alpha$ is the classical PBW rank: the dimension of the classical Serre enveloping-algebra component. No nondegeneracy or freeness of the divided-power lattice is asserted or used.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite symmetric Cartan matrix, its generic Serre quotient, its actual divided-power subalgebra and the finite ordinary words in each root degree.

[F1] Quantum factorials are nonzero rational functions; the symmetric Gaussian coefficients are Laurent polynomials, satisfy $\binom mr_t[m-r]_t=\binom m{r+1}_t[r+1]_t$, and obey $\sum_{r=0}^m(-1)^r\binom mr_t t^{\pm(m-1)r}=0$ for $m\ge1$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]). The cross identity is direct factorial cancellation. The positive-exponent alternating identity is the Gauss product at $z=-1$; substituting $t^{-1}$ and using $[n]_{t^{-1}}=[n]_t$ gives the negative-exponent identity.

[F2] The abstract separate Serre half embeds as the actual negative half, without any choice principle ([[lem-the-generic-borel-half-and-opposite-half-form-a-dj-crossed-double]]). Its divided-power subalgebra consists exactly of finite $A$-linear combinations of products of $f_i^n/[n]_t!$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]).

[F3] PBW for a supplied ordered finite or countable Lie basis is proved by terminating adjacent-inversion reduction and Jacobi. In a finite-word graded Lie presentation an ordered homogeneous basis can be obtained by retaining the first independent bracket words, without AC ([[lem-pbw-for-countably-presented-kac-moody-lie-algebras]]). The proof works over $\mathbb Q$ verbatim: its reductions use only field arithmetic and Jacobi.

[F4] For the classical complex Kac–Moody algebra, its negative half is the Lie algebra on the negative simple generators with exactly the separate negative Serre relations ([[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]). Thus the classical PBW rank here means the same $\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^-)[-\alpha]$ as in the existing generic-rank theorem.

exported_sections_exact.Statement: Let $L$ be a complex Lie algebra with a supplied finite or countable ordered basis $(x_i)$. The products $x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_m}$ with $i_1\le\cdots\le i_m$, including $1$ for $m=0$, form a basis of $U(L)$. Consequently $L\to U(L)$ is injective. For the finite-word graded algebras here, compatible homogeneous bases of subalgebras and quotients can be obtained without AC.

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
Let $Q=p^a>1$, $\nu=\sqrt Q$, and $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)\subset\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal H$ be the real twisted Hall algebra of the finite-dimensional nilpotent representations of a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_Q$; an acyclic quiver needs no nilpotence restriction. Write $u_i=[S_i]$ for its vertex simples and $C_K$ for the $K$-algebra they generate. Let $A=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, and let $U_A^-$ be the generic divided-power integral half for the symmetric matrix $a_{ij}=2\delta_{ij}-(\text{number of arrows joining }i,j)$.

There is a surjective graded algebra map
$$\Psi:K\otimes_{A,t\mapsto\nu^{-1}}U_A^-\longrightarrow C_K,\qquad F_i\longmapsto u_i.$$
It preserves the homogeneous form $(Q-1)^{-\operatorname{ht}\alpha}B_{\nu^{-1}}$. In particular $\dim_K C_K[\alpha]$ is at most the classical PBW rank. This conclusion requires only positive Green pairing and the generic word-form identity, and does not require specialized nondegeneracy or any numerical Serre-presentation comparison.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The indicated quiver Hall algebra, its simple classes and composition algebra, the integral half and the specialization parameter.

[F1] The selected quiver category is a finite-field hereditary Hall category by [[lem-finite-loopless-quiver-nilpotent-category-is-hereditary-finitary]]. Its simple Euler values symmetrize to the displayed Cartan matrix. The Green coproduct in [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]] makes each vertex simple primitive, since it has only the zero subobject and itself. The Green form is $([M],[N])_H=\delta_{[M],[N]}/|\operatorname{Aut}M|$, so its extension to finite real sums is positive definite. Its homogeneous adjunction is compatible with the primitive braided coproduct on words in vertex simples, with twist $\nu^{(\alpha,\beta)}$, vacuum norm $1$ and simple norms $1/(Q-1)$ ([[prop-green-hall-pairing-is-nondegenerate]], [[thm-green-hall-coproduct-is-a-twisted-bialgebra-map]]). Here the primitive assertion refers to the root-graded braided Hall coproduct, before adjoining the torus.

[F2] The actual generic symmetric half has the uniquely normalized homogeneous form $B_t$ defined by the matching-permutation formula on ordinary words. Its adjunction is primitive first-letter deletion with tensor twist $t^{-(\alpha,\beta)}$ and simple norms $1$. Ordinary-word values are Laurent polynomials; divided-power products have only finite products of symmetric quantum factorials as denominators. In each degree, the finite ordinary-word Gram matrix $G_\alpha(t)$ satisfies $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q(c)}G_\alpha(c)\le p_\alpha$ at every positive real $c$, where $p_\alpha$ is the classical PBW rank. These assertions, including actual Serre-quotient descent, are proved in [[lem-finite-serre-word-form-and-classical-rank-bound]].

[F3] The integral half $U_A^-$ is the actual $A$-subalgebra of the generic half generated by $F_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_t!$. This is its definition in [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Quantum factorials have nonzero evaluations at $c=\nu^{-1}>0$; their symmetric quantum-integer factors are positive sums $c^{n-1}+c^{n-3}+\cdots+c^{1-n}$.

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A symmetrizable Cartan datum, a fixed $i\in I$, and the symmetric $q_i$-integer, factorial and Gaussian quotient from [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

[F1] $q_i=q^{d_i}$ for an indeterminate $q$ and positive integer $d_i$; all symmetric $q_i$-factorials in the quotient are nonzero ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F2] $R[z]$ is the polynomial ring over a commutative ring $R$, and $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ consists of finite Laurent sums with integer coefficients ([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]).

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
Fix a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $A^+$ and $A^-$ be the independently presented $k$-algebras on $e_i$ and $f_i$, respectively, modulo their separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, and let $C=k[P^\vee]$ have basis $K_h$, $h\in P^\vee$. Then the vector space
$$D=A^-\otimes_k C\otimes_k A^+$$
carries a unique associative unital algebra structure in which $a_-\otimes K_h\otimes a_+$ equals the product of the three embedded factors, the factors retain their algebra structures, and
$$K_h e_i=q^{\alpha_i(h)}e_iK_h,\qquad K_h f_i=q^{-\alpha_i(h)}f_iK_h,\qquad [e_i,f_j]=\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$
This is the Drinfeld–Jimbo crossed double. Its normal-factor multiplication map to the presented algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is an algebra isomorphism, whose inverse sends $E_i,F_i,K_h$ to the indicated factor generators. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective; their images are the subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

In the presentation $\widetilde U$ obtained by omitting both Serre families, the halves $T^\pm$ are free, the toral factor is $C$, and multiplication identifies $\widetilde U=T^-\otimes C\otimes T^+$. Every Serre element satisfies
$$[F_k,S^+_{ij}]=[E_k,S^-_{ij}]=0.$$
Writing $I^\pm\trianglelefteq T^\pm$ for the separate Serre ideals, the full Serre ideal of $\widetilde U$ is exactly
$$I^-\otimes C\otimes T^+ + T^-\otimes C\otimes I^+.$$
No nonsingularity of the Cartan matrix and no choice principle is required.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite symmetrizable Cartan datum and its Drinfeld–Jimbo presentation.

[F1] The toral, toral-action and mixed relations give the Serre-free presentation; adding the separate Serre sums gives $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, and assignments satisfying these relations extend uniquely ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]], [[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

[F2] The integral weight characters are additive, $q_i=q^{d_i}$, and $q_j^{a_{ji}}=q_i^{a_{ij}}$ by symmetrizability ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

[F3] For $t=q_i$, the symmetric Gaussian coefficients satisfy $C_{N,r}[N-r]_i=C_{N,r+1}[r+1]_i$ and $\sum_{s=0}^N(-1)^s C_{N,s}t^{\pm(N-1)s}=0$ for $N\ge1$. The first identity is factorial cancellation and the second follows from the Gauss formula and its inverse-parameter substitution ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]).

[F4] Tensoring quotient maps is surjective and has kernel the sum of the factor kernels, by repeated right exactness ([[thm-right-exactness-of-tensor-products]]).

[F5] The positive, negative and toral subalgebras are the generated images of the corresponding presentation generators ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
On the direct-sum Hall space define
$$ ([M],[N])_G=\frac{\delta_{[M],[N]}}{a_M}. $$
This bilinear form is nondegenerate over $\mathbb Q(\nu)$ and satisfies
$$ ([M]\star[N],[R])_G =([M]\otimes[N],\Delta'([R]))_{G\otimes G}, $$
where the tensor pairing is the product of the two Green pairings.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite-field hereditary Hall category and the Hall basis.

[F1] $a_M$ is a finite positive integer and the Green coproduct has coefficient $\nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}P^R_{M,N}/a_R$ ([[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]]).

[F2] $P^R_{M,N}=a_Ma_Ng^R_{M,N}$ ([[lem-hall-sequence-count-equals-aut-weighted-subobject-count]]).

exported_sections_exact.Statement:
For a finite-field hereditary Hall category, products of Green images converge
coefficientwise and
$$ \Delta'([M]\star[N])=\Delta'([M])\cdot\Delta'([N]) $$
in the completion of [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]], where the
target multiplication is the stated Euler-twisted tensor multiplication. The
coproduct is coassociative and counital by
[[lem-green-hall-coproduct-is-coassociative]]. It is not asserted that the
whole completion is an algebra.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite-field hereditary Hall category and basis objects $M,N$.

[F1] The basis formulas for $\Delta'$, the twisted Hall product and twisted tensor multiplication are those of [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]].

[F2] Products $\Delta'([M])\cdot\Delta'([N])$ have finite coefficient sums ([[lem-green-coproduct-products-converge]]).

[F3] The cross–square identity holds for the four external objects ([[lem-green-cross-square-counting-identity]]).

[F4] The Euler form is additive on $K_0$ ([[lem-hall-euler-form-is-additive]]).

[F5] Endpoint-labelled exact-sequence counts and Hall numbers satisfy $P^R_{A,B}=a_Aa_Bg^R_{A,B}$ ([[lem-hall-sequence-count-equals-aut-weighted-subobject-count]]).

exported_sections_exact.Statement: For a finite symmetrizable GCM over $\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak r^\pm$ is the ideal of the free half $\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^\pm$ generated by $(\operatorname{ad}e_i)^{1-a_{ij}}e_j$ or $(\operatorname{ad}f_i)^{1-a_{ij}}f_j$, respectively, for $i\ne j$. Hence $\mathfrak g(A)$ has exactly the Cartan relations and both Serre families as a presentation. Its halves have the corresponding separate Serre presentations, and multiplication gives the vector-space isomorphism $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak h)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)\cong U(\mathfrak g)$.
exported_sections_exact.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The symmetrizable Serre quotient and its vanishing residual kernel.

[F1] The quotient by both Serre families is g(A). ([[lem-the-serre-quotient-has-weyl-symmetry-and-no-residual-kac-moody-kernel]]).

[F2] PBW applies to the homogeneous bases. ([[lem-pbw-for-countably-presented-kac-moody-lie-algebras]]).
